Memory Applicability Guard.

A decision-support prototype for checking whether stored memory should shape an agent's next answer or action.

RoleIndependent projectPeriodMay—August 2026StackPython · JSON · Unit tests
MEMORY GUARD / DECISION MAPCONTEXT → ACTION
UUseCURRENT + RELEVANT
IIgnoreSTALE OR REVOKED
AAskEVIDENCE GAP

The case / 03

Long-term memory can make an assistant more useful, but a remembered preference or permission may be outdated, unrelated, or revoked. The prototype makes that decision explicit before the memory influences a recommendation or action.

What I built

I created a research-informed Python decision helper that evaluates a candidate memory against the present request and returns a structured result. Its response distinguishes when to use the memory, ignore it, or ask the user for clarification.

Decisions that mattered

  • Check applicability before personalization. A fact can be true and still be irrelevant to the current task.
  • Respect changed permissions. Revoked instructions must not quietly survive as an old preference.
  • Make uncertainty visible. When evidence is missing, the safer decision is often to clarify.

Validation and limits

The helper is packaged as an installable agent skill and checked with deterministic tests. It is a decision-support research prototype, not a production-validated autonomous safety system. The visual above describes the decision branches rather than showing a live interface.
